newsitem.title: TUNISIA: Tunisia gives offshore firms larger market access.
newsitem.headline: Tunisia gives offshore firms larger market access.

text.p: Offshore companies established in Tunisia will get a larger access for their products in the domestic market as part of the country's efforts to attract foreign investment, Tunisian President Zine al-Abidine Ben Ali announced on Thursday.

"We have given instructions for a review of the system that currently governs these (offshore) companies and that prevents them from selling more than 20 percent of their production on the domestic market," Ben Ali said in a speech at the occasion of the 9th anniversary of his arrival to power.

"It is natural that we should give Tunisian and foreign companies set up in our country and producing entirely for export, priority access to the domestic market to back up the effort they are making to create jobs and the contribution they are making in favor of the nation's economy," he said.

More than a thousand companies with foreign or mixed capital are currently in operation in Tunisia, of which 875 are devoted entirely for export, mainly in the textile, mechanical and electrical industry, chemicals and food processing.

Ben Ali said that between his arrival to power in 1987 and 1995, foreign investment in Tunisia totalled 2.7 billion dinars ($2.75 billion) for the setting up of more than 840 industrial projects and the creation of over 56,000 new jobs.
